content.text: No liquidated damages or penalty mechanic runs against our side anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: redeem the Notes, in whole but not in part (the "Clean-Up Redemption") without any Make-Whole Payment (other than any Make-Whole Payments already due and payable on such date)
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee on the Issuer or Depositor in favour of Cellco, so the preferred position is met. The only premium-style amount is the Make-Whole Payment (Sections 8.1-8.2; definition at Appendix A), which is a yield-maintenance amount payable to Noteholders on a voluntary Optional Redemption elected by the Class A Certificateholder and funded through the agreed waterfall — it is investor economics, not a breach-triggered liquidated sum payable to the counterparty, and the Clean-Up Redemption is expressly available without any Make-Whole Payment. The other amounts we reviewed run the right way or are ordinary compensation: late fees, prepayment charges and other Supplemental Servicing Fees are collected from Obligors rather than paid by us; servicing-transition expenses are "paid by the resigning or terminated Servicer"; the Successor Servicer's $150,000 appointment fee is third-party compensation paid from the waterfall, not a penalty; and the indemnities in Section 6.3 run from the Servicer and Marketing Agent to us. No redline is warranted.
